title: for the basename-only writers, does the module's own directory constant name the reader directory?

population_source.population_definition: rows of E487 class in {direct,helper,loop} with directory_class == the basename-only class

fold_rule.literal: a string constant that carries '/' is a path
fold_rule.name: module-level and same-function assignments are folded up to 12 hops
fold_rule.join: os.path.join(a, b, ...) folds as the cartesian concatenation; the repo root folds to the empty string so the first part is written repo-relative
fold_rule.add: a + b folds when both sides fold to strings
fold_rule.file: os.path.dirname(...(os.path.abspath(__file__))) folds to the module's own parent, walked up once per dirname wrapper
fold_rule.alias: alias.NAME folds into that module's own binding when the module exists in this repository and is imported by this file; a third-party module is unresolved

class_definition.the_module_directory_expression_names_th: a folded directory path equals the directory the reader resolves to
class_definition.the_module_directory_expression_names_an: a folded directory path is a strict ancestor of the reader's directory, so the subdirectory is named somewhere this fold does not follow
class_definition.the_module_directory_expression_names_a_: the module folds directory paths and none is the reader's directory or an ancestor of it: the writer is placed somewhere else
class_definition.the_module_states_a_directory_expression: the module has directory-shaped constants but none folds to a path (argv, os.environ, parameters, dict keys)
class_definition.the_module_states_no_directory_expressio: the module has no directory-shaped constant at all

method_limits: the fold reads one module per tracing source and follows one hop into an imported repository module; a directory built from a function parameter, argv, os.environ or a dict key is published unresolved, never as a directory statement
K_OTHER is a positive statement only when a folded path exists; a module that folds nothing is K_UNRESOLVED or K_NONE

K_SAME says the module names the reader's directory, not that the write happens there at run time: the write path itself was traced by E487 to a bare basename, so a runtime-composed suffix can still differ
the population is E487's basename-only arm, kept byte-for-byte as published; this face adds a directory question and does not re-open the parent's class question

the repo root folds to the empty string because these modules compute ROOT from __file__; a module that hardcodes a relative path is compared repo-relative too, so both spellings land on the same string
